Definition: of Hebrew origin (H6162); a pledge, i.e. part of the purchase-money or property given in advance as security for the rest:--earnest.
BiblicalUsage: The earnest is a pledge, the first part of the payment given in advance to guarantee the rest. God has sealed us and given the earnest of the Spirit in our hearts, He has wrought us for immortality and given us the earnest of the Spirit, and the Spirit is the earnest of our inheritance until the redemption of the purchased possession.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the earnest is the most comforting word in the New Testament for a doubting Christian: God does not ask us to wait for the whole payment on trust alone, He puts the Spirit in our hearts now as the first instalment. What He has begun He will finish, and I hold that the Spirit's presence in us is the guarantee of it.
